utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The witness to be called today is one for whom protective measures in advance had been sought and obtained. He's been here over the weekend, and there is no further application for him to be protected. He's prepared to give evidence in full open session. Over the weekend, obviously, a lot of work has been done with him, and those in the Prosecution team doing that work have taken every step they can to make all material that's appropriate available to the Defence as soon as it's come into our hands in usable form. That's led to, I think, the serving of probably a couple of proofing summaries, and I hope that the Chamber now has something headed "An Amended Proofing Summary." A number of exhibits have also been produced to the Defence, I think some of them without any form of translation. I'd rather get them across to them in the original B/C/S than not at all. We've been troubled to some degree over the weekend by a significant computer problem with one of the databases, or something to that effect, so that it hasn't been possible, simply, to identify or to extract all the documents that we might have wished to do. The consequence is that the production of exhibits may be a little less smooth today than I would normally want, but I'll do the best I can to keep things absolutely chronological, because my judgement is that that helps you most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Why were the exhibits only being produced at the weekend?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if a witness comes in, there is a process of proofing -- well, not over the weekend but before the weekend -- matters may arise which are of significance and which won't be known about until then. Therefore, if they are only known about then -- and this is a witness, as the Court will know, who came, I think, with a subpoena, so that the materiality of documents simply isn't known in advance, and once it is known, they have to be extracted. There is simply no other way of dealing with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is not a case where he has brought the exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Some he has brought, and they've been handed over. Other exhibits become relevant, from either his documents or from things that he tells us about; they then have to be extracted. And if the relevant part of the database is in difficulty, there's nothing we can do. But we're working as fast as we can to get everything available. I'm most concerned to ensure that material comes to you in a way that's helpful to you and not at random.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Where we will be asking him to comment on -- if and where I will be asking him to comment on documents that have already been produced, I'm not intending to produce further copies of the same documents. It seems to me that that's both wasteful and probably ultimately more confusing for you. If I'm wrong about that, and you tell me, I'll adjust for future witnesses. But at the moment, if a document's been produced as a Prosecution Exhibit already, I'll refer to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Naumovski?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you, Your Honours. When the Chamber ruled on protective measures of these witnesses who have asked for protective measures, I was a bit confused, because I think that in that way, the Chamber has done something that is really contrary to the equality of arms. However, I believe that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That is not so. We bore all those matters in mind when we made the order. Now, is there anything you want to raise about the --

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Yes, Your Honours, this was just a preliminary remark. The integrity of the witness was to be protected as much as possible, and I understand that. However, it is the second time now, as was the case with the first confidential witness, as with this one, that a whole set of protective measures is introduced, including limiting the number of Defence counsel who can ask questions, and then the witness changes his mind and decides not to seek protective measures. I think that this is not a person who actually changed their mind, because I think that he wants publicity. However, since this is happening for the second time, the Defence of Dario Kordic believes that the Prosecution has actually abused the procedural issues, because it is not -- this is not an issue of protective measures -- that is, of protecting his identity -- but rather to introduce an element of surprise against the Defence, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Naumovski, what are you asking us to do? Because let's get on with the evidence, if we can, rather than complaining. Now, what motion or application are you making? What has happened is -- let me finish. What has happened is this witness asked for these measures; we granted them. He has changed his mind, and the position is now that he's going to give evidence in open court. Now, is there any application you want to make?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Yes, I will submit our application right away, and then I have an additional one which I need to clarify. Since this witness has now become a witness who will testify in open court, and since we believe that this is an abuse of the procedure, we ask that this witness not be allowed to testify today, because we were supposed to be given the evidentiary material by 17 May. Secondly, we received an outline of this witness's testimony last week, that is, Friday. And the period from Friday to midnight last night, we received an additional 150 pages of evidentiary material. Mr. Kordic was not even able to read through this material, let alone sit down with his Defence counsel and discuss the issues which this raises. So we were twice -- since we were not able to either read through this material nor discuss it with Mr. Kordic, who received it at the last moment, our request, should the Trial Chamber not grant the first request, is to allow the Defence additional time for our cross-examination. And I don't have in mind just a couple of days, because a couple of days will not be enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us see how we get on. Let the witness give his evidence in chief, and then we'll see how much of it you claim not to have had disclosed to you, and we'll review the position at the end of the evidence in chief. If you're going to ask time before you cross-examine, we will consider that application. But let us get on with the witness now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I have just one more matter to raise regarding the ruling of the Chamber regarding the six protected witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It doesn't relate to this witness, I take it. We'll hear any applications you have about other witnesses after the witness's evidence, when we're at a convenient moment during the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I'm not going to not belabour the point. I think that one matter has not been clarified. Pursuant to the Chamber ruling of 19 March regarding classification of this witness as a special protected witness, we received a very small portion of the testimony about ten days ago, and then we received the rest of the material over the weekend, and we had nothing. For this reason, we are just simply not prepared. We're not ready to cross-examine this witness. And I have a similar request as my colleague. If we cannot -- we need to be -- we are asking either this witness not be called now, or alternatively, that we be given additional time to prepare for the cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll hear the examination in chief, and then we'll decide whether time is needed for cross-examination. Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can I simply explain in one sentence? The witness came here, the subpoena duces tecum. There is no duty for disclosure that has not been complied with. On the contrary, in accordance with my normal practice, the Defence have had a great deal more than the Rules require of me. As soon as I've known that documents might be of importance or might be of help to them, I've ordered them to be transmitted, even untranslated or whatever, so that they can consider them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's have the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. The witness is going back on Wednesday, and I'll deal with that later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you would like to take a seat. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your full name, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Stjepan Kljuic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were born in 1939. Are you a citizen of Bosnia and Herzegovina, your ethnicity and religion being, please?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: I was a citizen of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I was born in Sarajevo. My ethnic origin is Croatian, and I'm Catholic, Roman Catholic, by religion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Educated in philosophy at Zagreb and Sarajevo. We're going to deal with what happened in the early '90s, but are you presently the president of the Republican Party in Bosnia and Herzegovina, that being a multi-ethnic and independent party founded by you on the 5th of June, 1994?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes. I studied philosophy and literature in Zagreb briefly and then in Sarajevo. For 35 years, I was a journalist and a dissident in a Communist society, and today I'm the leader of a party with a civic orientation, and I want to explain what that means. It is pro-western, secular, democratic, and I'm a member of the parliament of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the HDZ party founded on the 18th of August of 1990, with Davor Perinovic the first president and you a founding member?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: I took part in preparations for the establishment of the HDZ on 18 August 1990, but the day and night before that we had comprehensive discussions with guests from Zagreb who arrived in Sarajevo to found the Bosnian-Herzegovinian HDZ. I was a leader of a group of Sarajevo intellectuals, and among the guests from Zagreb were, very briefly, Josip Manolic, president of the Croatian government, and then continuously Miljenko Zagar, general secretary of the HDZ in Zagreb; Dalibor Brozovic, a member of the academy and a high official with the HDZ; the late Gojko Susak, who at that time was on duty of Minister of Immigration with the government of Croatia, and many other guests from Zagreb who were of lesser stature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In September of 1990, did Perinovic, the first president, come to be replaced? Just "Yes" or "No" to that.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did President Tudjman say anything to you about that before it happened?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: On my way to Germany, I passed through Zagreb on 5th and 6th September 1990, and I was taken to Dr. Tudjman on that occasion. I then learned, in a conversation with him, that Perinovic was going to be replaced, because as early as 17 August, I said that Perinovic could not be leader of the Croatian people. However, they replaced him because it was determined that he was an ethnic Serb. When I argued against Perinovic's presidency, it was not only because he was an ethnic Serb, but politically speaking, he was not the right person to take the Croatian people to the first democratic elections. On WDR Radio in Germany, I learned that Perinovic was replaced and that I was named the general secretary and acting president.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you happy with your appointment taking place without democratic process or not?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: I was mostly pleased for Perinovic having been replaced, and I took this appointment as a great challenge because there was very little time left before the elections and the Croatian policy in Bosnia-Herzegovina needed to be spelled out. Today, I think that I was fortunate to have become the president of the HDZ at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your position ever to be subject to election by the party?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: We copied the statute of the HDZ party in Croatia, and there it was said very clearly that the president could only be elected by the convention. But there was no time to call for a new convention because you had to bear in mind that there were only 70 days left until the elections. I insisted that my appointment be done in Sarajevo so that I would demonstrate the autonomy of the Bosnian-Herzegovinian HDZ. When we won the elections in great style, I organised a convention of the HDZ, created a platform for the political activity of the Croatian people of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and received acceptance for both my position as president and the platform for the policy by acclamation. After the elections, I became a member of the presidency based on the relative majority of votes which we received.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you can probably deal with this next question by just the answer "Yes" if the proposition is correct. Paragraph 9 of the summary. Did you win 44 of the 240 seats in parliament, gaining two seats on the presidency, you and Franjo Boras; did you achieve some 23 per cent of the major governmental and state industry positions, including six ministerial and eight deputy ministerial posts, with majorities in 10 municipalities where Croats were not, in fact, in a majority, those municipalities including Mostar, Derventa, Bugojno, Fojnica, Zepce, Kotor Varos, in which place, or some of which, I think, the Croat representation was only 17 per cent? Is what I've just read out to you correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes, except that in all the municipalities where we won, the total percentage of the Croatian population was 17,3. I must say that this was an exceptional result, because in the previous Communist government, the Croats were only represented by 7,4 per cent in the government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you look, please, at the first exhibit in time, which I think just precedes the elections, and I think we have bundles produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It may be that some documents will have to be fitted within this if a strict chronological sequence is to be followed. Nevertheless, I hope this will be a more convenient method than handing documents in one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: May it please the Court, part of the problem announced by Mr. Naumovski is that these are new to us, some of them, and only in one language, not in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, let's see how we get on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What I will ask of the witness, with documents that aren't in translation, is that he lays them or has them laid on the ELMO, and if he can be shown how to use the pointer. Thank you very much. He can point to the passages of the documents of which he may speak. It is, of course, important, these documents having arrived, that they are properly produced by this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Nice, the Rules are that documents have to be in the working languages of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Of course, yes. I have to tell you that there is simply no available translation service over the weekends, and it's as simple as that. We can't deal with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, but it places difficulties for everybody --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Of course it does, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- if documents are produced in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I quite understand that, but this is the best that we can do. Of course, the translations are on their way. They have been or are being submitted for translation straightaway, and there are original language speakers on both sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, that may be, but the Rules provide for a way of doing these things, and what you're doing is technically applying for an exception.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, it may be, but if the witness comes with his documents under the subpoena and I cannot provide translations overnight, and I can't, then the alternatives are stark. Either the witness can't give his evidence or he can give his evidence and talk about the original document, because he understands it and, of course, the defendants themselves will understand it, and whatever he says by way of -- whatever he says is the meaning of a particular passage will no doubt be susceptible to some form of verification, because we have the interpreters simultaneously translating for us in the booths, and will be further confirmed when the written documents are provided later in English and French. (Trial Chamber confers)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document dated the 8th of October, 1990, just tell us, in a word or phrase, what is it?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: First of all, gentlemen, I wanted to say three things at the beginning. I have come here under subpoena, not of my own free will, and I am forced to cooperate with you by the laws of my country, Bosnia and Herzegovina. Thirdly, I asked to speak in open session because what I am saying is part of my political struggle, and it is no secret. Everything I tell you today is what I have already said several times in my political speeches and interviews. This meeting took place after I was elected acting president in Sarajevo on the 16th of September. All municipal and other organisations had to be brought together before the elections, and that's why we gathered in Sarajevo, so that I could get to know them and they could get to know me. For the sake of continuity of political activity, the representatives of the HDZ from Zagreb were also present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to take matters shortly. Will you turn now to the third sheet of this document, where at the foot of the page we see your name. Does this document set out what you said at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes. This confirms that on the 17th of April, a day before the establishment of the Bosnian and Herzegovinian HDZ, I was present at all these discussions and wanted to help, but they did not accept what I said. And Perinovic ignored a whole group of people who were able, who were intellectuals, who had been Croatian dissidents during Communism, and without whom the party could not exist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, on this occasion, and you can take this quite shortly by looking at this sheet or turning over to the following sheet, what on this occasion did you set out of your own political position? If you want to turn over to the following sheet, Mr. Kljuic, you can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I wonder if it would be helpful if we had translated what is against the witness's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Certainly, if the interpreters are equipped with a copy in the booths, or alternatively following it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Kljuic has to read it; otherwise we are not allowed to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Would you read it, then, Mr. Kljuic, please, just read what follows "Dr. Stjepan Kljuic, Sarajevo, politicki tajnik." Can you read it out, please?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. [Translation of Serbo-Croatian document as read] "He introduced himself personally and stressed that on the 17th of March, he had joined the HDZ party wishing to help the former leadership with a stronger personnel, group of people, which they did not accept. Perinovic ignored a group of people who were willing to put themselves to the disposal of the party and to work, which was then a sign that certain things were not going in the right direction, Mr. Kljuic said." And there is an error here. It is not the 17th of March but the 17th of August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Carry on, please. It goes over to the next --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: [Translation of Serbo-Croatian document as read] "After that, he set out a part of the programme of the party for the future, stressing that a person can be respectable and the leader, according to what he does, and that a list of meetings would be drawn up, and that work would be coordinated from the centre. The HDZ is a global party, fighting for the interests of the Croatian people throughout the world, and certain games are of a non-party character. Political theses are to be drawn up to which everyone will have to adhere, and party discipline will have to be respected. The statutes will have to be adapted to the political norms of life in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Article 18 of the Statute has made everything that has happened valid. All the presidents of the steering committees are to be gathered together, and they are to agree on their work. The same mistakes must not be allowed to recur. From tomorrow, the office will be open, and there is work waiting for us, so that there is no place for mutual discord and dissatisfaction, Stjepan Kljuic said."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's Exhibit 2719. Can we turn to next document, please, 2720, which comes in two parts, I think. The first part is the conclusions of the presidency of the 15th of October; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think the second part, which is dated the 5th of November, is, I think, the minutes for a meeting , not the minutes, the -- well, you tell us what it is, better than I ask you. What's the second part, starting on the 5th of November, third sheet?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: This is a meeting of the presidency of the HDZ, a regular meeting during the election campaign, at which the acting president was present, all the vice-presidents, the treasurer, the administrative secretary, and some members of the municipal committees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you produced those documents for the time being, and I may not ask you any detailed questions about them, but one can see -- we can see that the name "Kostroman" appears. Just tell us, what was Kostroman's role in these early stages, and what was his position generally?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: First I have to say that I was duty-bound to bring with me the documents I had. This document is not important, but Ignac Kostroman was a person who was in the leadership with Perinovic, and I inherited him. He was the technical secretary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were his views generally? What was his position generally?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: I can't talk about his views, because, as president, I did not pay much attention to him. But I can say that later on, he went to Herceg-Bosna and that our ways parted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I go back to the amended proofing summary at paragraph 10. Did you view the HDZ BiH as an independent party, or not?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: I considered and advocated the HDZ being an independent party, but a sister party with the party in Zagreb. That is why I insisted that it should be called "the HDZ of Bosnia and Herzegovina." There were suggestions that it should be called "the HDZ for Bosnia-Herzegovina." Apart from this, as president, I registered the party at the high court in Sarajevo, with the stamp and signature of the president, and it was valid, as such, and was able to take part in the first democratic elections in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was President Tudjman of Croatia in any position to represent the party of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Later on, there were talks between the leaders of all the Yugoslav republics. Unfortunately, Bosnia and Herzegovina was not represented by representatives of the Muslims, Serbs, and the Croats, but only by the president of the presidency, Mr. Izetbegovic. So I asked Dr. Tudjman, at these Yugoslav talks, since there was no representative of the Bosnia-Herzegovinian Croats there, that he should represent our interests.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Tudjman's view of the independence of your party coincide with your view, or did he hold a different view?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: In the end, he conceded independence for our party, but of course, we were two sister parties. Formally he recognised the independence of the party, but we were connected by all the other elements: The media, our funds, the design of our symbols, and media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as the presidency of the HDZ, how were you regarded, as a president of the local party? How was Mr. Tudjman regarded in those terms?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Dr. Tudjman considered me the president of the HDZ of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I confirmed this status, not only by leading the party, but by acquiring legitimacy because I was elected to the presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And later on, at the convention in Mostar on the 23rd and 24th of March, 1991, I gained overwhelming support and was elected the regular president. This convention confirmed my political platform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did people like Boban accept you as the true president of the party?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: I must say that at that time, Boban did not represent any force within the HDZ. He was one of the 44 deputies in the parliament, and he is remembered by the fact that he never took the floor. In Mostar, at the convention, I gave a two-hour break, thus giving the counter-candidates a chance to consolidate. At the beginning, there were several candidates running against me, but they soon they gave up. The representatives of the municipalities from Herzegovina withdrew to a separate room, and when they took a count, they saw that they numbered only 53, and some of them were in favour of me, so that they stood no chance of getting Boban voted for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're slightly running ahead of the question I wanted an answer to. It's just that -- did Boban and people like him accept you as the true president, or did they look elsewhere for authority? You can probably deal with it at that stage quite shortly, or very shortly.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Some of them personally did not accept me as president, because in our behaviour and philosophy and world view, we represented two different worlds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next exhibit, please, 2721. There's only one paragraph of this we want, but perhaps you'll tell us first of all what the document is. It's slightly out of chronology, because this is back in the 9th of January of 1991. What is the document, please?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Immediately after winning the elections, we had to change the strategy of work of the party. In the first stage, we focused only on the elections, but when we gained power, we had to appoint a large number of people to high positions. We had to take these positions, and most people were amateurs, with no experience in government. And then we looked for ways to take over power legally as soon as possible and to act in a legal manner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this document set something out? It's headed "Programme," I see.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was a practical document with brief instructions on how we should act now, after the elections, in the first stage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second sheet, Number 6, please. If you would just read it out for us, then we'll hear in English or French what the interpreters provide.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: [Translation of Serbo-Croatian document as read] "Closer contact must urgently be established with the leadership in Zagreb by the overall leadership of the party in order to agree on the coordination and synchronisation of the HDZ, and meetings have to be organised to this end. The person who should execute this is the president in agreement with the leadership." May I comment on this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: You should know that at that time, in Croatia, the HDZ was already in power, and the party coordination was needed not only politically but a large number of municipalities in which we had won the elections had local connections, direct local connections with the Republic of Croatia, and many things had to be furthered. Let me just mention employment, transport, the building of joint projects such as waterworks, irrigation canals, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next series of exhibits in the Court's and my learned friends' papers are produced by the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The next series of exhibits in the papers for the Court and for my learned friends are produced under the subpoena. Apart from identifying what they are, I don't wish to make any points through the witness in relation to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Kljuic, will you just look, please, at the series of documents and confirm what they are. Z2723, does that record a meeting of the presidency of the party on the 15th of January, 1991? No comment is required beyond telling me that that is correct, if it is correct.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- is the 25th of January, '91, directions issued by you to municipal committees?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 2725 is a pronouncement of the 25th of January?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: The 25th of January.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 25th of January, and the subject matter? The title?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Public announcement because of the military threat against the Republic of Croatia. This is a very important document because it was published after a forged film by the Yugoslav intelligence service, the KOS, about the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Croatia, General Martin Spegelj. This was produced by Belgrade propaganda, and in it, the Croats were represented as the aggressors, as those responsible for the break-up of Yugoslavia. They were represented as being very well armed, and the film was supposed to incite hatred, and not only among Serbs against the Croats, but also in all the other republics. Since the Republic of Croatia was in a really difficult situation, I appeared on television and read out this announcement, where I said that if the Republic of Croatia is attacked, we, Croats from Bosnia and Herzegovina, would stand in its defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: I have to say that that's what happened. When the war in Croatia started, many Croats from Bosnia and Herzegovina actively joined in the defence of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document, 2726, a letter from Pero Markovic to you and to Franjo Boras. The title of the letter?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: [Translation of Serbo-Croatian document as read] "Report on certain events which took place last weekend in the municipality of Capljina."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document, 2727, 29th of January. I think this is a record, is it, of a meeting of the presidency held on that day?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 2728, dated the 2nd of February of 1991, a letter from an individual to you and to Ivancic. It's in the bundle, but you don't make any point out of it?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: The document is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next one is 2729, which is the 5th of February, 1991, the conclusions of the HDZ Mostar municipal committee.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: This is a very interesting document which speaks of the loyalty of the Mostar HDZ in Bosnia and Herzegovina. It says -- okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 2730 is a letter of Kovac, president of the municipal assembly, to you, dated the 12th of February?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is support to me, personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Back to the summary at paragraph 11. You've already told us something, I think, of the convention held at Mostar on the 24th and 25th of March, and I needn't ask you more about that. Of the 288 representatives, what number were from Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Fifty-three.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of proportions, how does that assist us? Is there any significance in that proportion?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: It was on a par with the share of the Croat population or the Mostar Croats in the population of Bosnian Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that meeting attended by people from Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Namely?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susak first, then Mr. Beljo, who was the HDZ secretary general of Croatia, and a number of others less prominent. But there were quite a number of people from Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the true role of those people?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: I must say that they helped to deal with the extremists, but to tame the extremist part of the HDZ which was really unduly ambitious, and they extended their full support to me, but that was also due to the support that I enjoyed among the present representatives of the Croat people. Had I not enjoyed such support, they perhaps would have acted differently. But as it was, they simply had no choice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you speak of an extremist part of the HDZ at this time, what, if any, clearly identifiable views did the extremist part hold that the majority or remaining part of the party did not hold?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: That is what I wanted to say. The Croat Democratic Union, as many other ethnic parties, was joined by quite a number of former Communists. Then the Yugoslav Intelligence Service also infiltrated its own people into it. As a result, no idea was accepted without resistance. Nonetheless, things were developing very quickly. Belgrade had a war programme, and other incidents had to be put to use. Besides, there is a certain parochial spirit in that area, that is, people who will never agree with anything, because, say, the same people who were against Perinovic subsequently turned against me, subsequently turned against Brkic. In other words, it is political destructiveness, and they could not really grasp -- they couldn't understand the historical conditions in which all this was taking place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the extremists' view was to what effect or conclusion?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: They simply wanted to foist upon us their own local policy as the party doctrine, and at the same time they never looked at what the reality was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should have asked you earlier, but I'll ask you now. What, in your experience, had been the relations between the different ethnic groups in Bosnia-Herzegovina generally?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: There is a tradition of tolerance amongst us. We inherited it from our parents. But this Serb fascism embodied in President Milosevic knew that they had an army which was the fourth conventional military force in Europe and believed that this would suffice to preserve the centralistic Yugoslavia. But Slovenia, Croatia and Bosnia were requesting a confederation in Yugoslavia in the early days, at an early stage, but when Milosevic refused that, he instrumentalised the media, the army, and the police to such an extent that it simply led to the resistance of non-Serb peoples. Naturally, this put an end to tolerance, as any newspaper, any television station, simply propagated -- proliferated hatred, chauvinism, racism, representing the Serbs as the only vulnerable people in the former Yugoslavia, although they were the only privileged people. At the moment when the war began in Slovenia and then in Croatia and in Bosnia, and you see it came to its end in Kosovo recently, the tolerance stopped, and now in Bosnia one has to look for people who are ready to come to grips with their hatred, and there are such people, and who are trusted also by representatives of other peoples and not only the one that they come from. So there was tolerance which was tolerable, which was bearable, until 1990, even idyllic in places, but the activation of the Serb fascism brought about great evil.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There are three major ethnic groupings. Croats, Serbs, and Muslims would create, I think, some four bilateral relations; that is, Serb-Croat, Serb-Muslim -- sorry, three -- Muslim-Croat. Was the tolerance as between those groups similar or was there any pronounced differences? For example, how was the Muslim-Croat relationship generally?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, to begin with, those relations were not always the same. During the Communist and royalist Yugoslavia, as the ruling people, the Serbs exercised more influence among the Muslims, and in consequence, during the Independent State of Croatia, that is, 1941 to 1945, the Muslims were informally in a state with Croats. The best relations in Bosnia-Herzegovina were between the Croats and the Muslims, in part because they were both under equal threat in Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Amended summary, at paragraph 12, was there the meeting on the 27th of March of 1991 between Tudjman and Milosevic, of which you became aware?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Everybody talks about that meeting, but I have no proof of it. All I have is what Mr. Stipe Mesic told me, and that is that together with Jovic, who was at that time the chairman or the presidency of Yugoslavia, arranged for some meeting between Tudjman, Milosevic, Jovic and Mesic, and yet later on this version was changed, and in all likelihood only Milosevic and Tudjman met on that occasion, and Mesic being eliminated from those talks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that meeting followed by other working group meetings of which you were aware?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Well, you'll know, and Mr. Bilandzic affirmed that here, that there were various meetings of working groups, but I knew nothing about that because I lived in Bosnia-Herzegovina and those took place in Belgrade and in Croatia. I mean we know about these matters from the writings from texts written in the territory of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take us, then, to April 1991 and a few more documents that you can deal with quite briefly. Document 2731, on which I need seek no detailed comment, is that a record or excerpts from a meeting of --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Yes, this is a digest, an excerpt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's the 4th of April of 1991. The next document --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- 2732, this is a letter dated the 8th of April from Dragutin Cicak. What is the subject matter of the letter, please?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Well, Dragutin Cicak was complaining against Dario Kordic. That was a staple practice there. They always -- there was always strife there. But as I was very busy as the president at that time, I could not really intervene very much or mediate between them, and it was of no importance for me. It was a local incident, and there were various such in various places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the first time that you've mentioned the name "Dario Kordic". When did you first become aware of him and in what setting?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: I believe I met him at meetings with municipal representatives, because in the beginning he was vice-president of the HDZ, while Dr. Barac was the president. Subsequently, Dr. Barac went to another duty and he became the president. I interceded to have him employed as a secretary for all national defence in the municipality of Busovaca, even though, in formal terms, he did not meet the terms. But he was young, and I believed that at that moment he could protect Croats and Muslims going to do their military service. As you must know, in 1990 and '91, the majority of Croats and Muslims from Bosnia were being sent to do their military service in Macedonia, Montenegro, and Serbia, and my thesis was to keep as many of them in Bosnia-Herzegovina or send them out only to Slovenia and Croatia because I thought it would be more promising to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that stage then, did you hold any views, one way or the other, about Kordic and his views or his ambition?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: It was of no consequence, from my point of view, as from the point of view as how I understood presidential duty. I simply had no time to go into that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just staying with document 2732, if you would turn to the second sheet just to explain the document to us, the first sheet is dated the 8th of April, the second sheet is the first of two typewritten sheets from Cicak. That one is dated the 7th. What's this second document?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: This is the first document of the 7th of April in which Cicak presumably addresses the municipal committee of the HDZ, and the second document he wrote was intended for me as the president of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Cicak like as a local politician, party worker, and so on?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Well, his attitude was correct. It is really very difficult to say how he was in the party, because that was an area which was quite quiet and quite safe. There were no Serbs there, only Muslims and Croats were there, and I paid more attention to where incidents were likely to happen and I really did not know how each and every municipal committee worked. That is only natural, because there were 67 organisations. I could not really keep them all under my control. However, it is quite obvious that those were personal conflicts, I should say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document is 2733. No points that I wish to make on it. Just identify it for what it is. This is dated the 16th of April, and is it excerpts of the minutes of the presidency?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: That is true, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document, 2734, again I don't desire to make any points. The 24th of April, a letter from you calling the first meeting of the HDZ BH main committee; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document, 2737, is this a document dated the 29th of May of 1991, and is it minutes of the third session of the party presidency that we --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes. I must have been away on a business trip somewhere, abroad perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your absence, by whom was the meeting chaired? The second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: At the first stage, Vitomir Lukic, he was my first vice-president, and after he died, Mate Boban became the first vice-president, and therefore he chaired the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we turn to the fourth sheet, the last sheet of this exhibit, we see that there's a signature of Kostroman and a stamp, your name, but no signature.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes, because I was not there, and they expected that I would read the record after my return and then confirm it. But Kostroman was the man who took notes and who signed it. But, sir, I mean this is not a political problem. Perhaps I had no time to read it. Had I read it, then I probably would have signed it. There is nothing disputable here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Paragraph 13 of the summary. In the course of your work on behalf of Bosnia-Herzegovina, did you meet a number or possibly all of the key personalities involved in the unfolding conflict, from Milosevic and Karadzic through to Lord Owen, Stoltenberg, and others?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was a very broad range of them. To begin with, the presidents of all Yugoslav republics and their delegates, then of course the meetings with Karadzic and Krajisnik from the Serb side, Izetbegovic and Behman from the Muslim side, and quite a number of international intermediaries, from Lord Owen to Jacques Santer, to a number of others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to deal next, please, paragraph 14 of the summary, with a meeting on the 13th of June of 1991 in Zagreb. What was the meeting?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: It was a regular meeting of representatives of HDZ of the Republic of Croatia and the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina. But you need to know that the circumstances at that time were already rather aggravated because it came in the wake of the incident at Plitvice and in Borovo Selo. At that time, the war in Croatia had not yet started, but everybody was already clear that it could not be prevented. The meeting was devoted to an analysis of the political situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina and preparation of some projects in case Bosnia-Herzegovina was recognised and in case Bosnia-Herzegovina was not recognised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. Nice, could we ask the witness, Mr. Kljuic, why was this meeting held in Zagreb rather than Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Answer Judge Bennouna's question, please.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes. I do not think this is of any consequence, because we held meetings alternatively in Zagreb and in Sarajevo very often during official visits of President Tudjman and Mr. Susak and some other ministers who came to Sarajevo, and then we would hold our meetings in Sarajevo, and we also held our regular meetings in Zagreb. So this was one of those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At your meetings in Zagreb, what level of representation from the Croatian government was there? Was it always President Tudjman himself or not?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: There are different kinds of meetings. As a statesman, I would come to pay an official visit to the Republic of Croatia as, for instance, when I was a guest of the Croatian diet on the occasion of the promulgation of the new Croatian constitution. Then I would be together with the president of the Bosnia-Herzegovina government, another member of the HDZ, Mr. Jure Pelivan, when we discussed inter-republican relations relative to economic matters, the port of Ploce, and so on and so forth. There were also some meetings which were only party meetings. This one was, one might say, a combination of all of that, because we first assessed the political situation and the security situation in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it was followed by a discussion on the activities of the party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke a little earlier, in answer to the question from the Judge, of meetings that were held alternatively in Zagreb and Sarajevo, suggesting that perhaps there was one type of meeting that was held in these two locations. If there was such a type of meeting, what representation from the government of Croatia or from the party in Croatia was there at the meetings held in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: A large number of meetings were attended in Zagreb. The topmost echelons of the Croatian state and the HDZ were represented, so President Tudjman, Prime Minister Manolic, Mesic, and Gregoric, or prime ministers, then minister Ramljak, and a number of others, and Mr. Susak. So that as usual, usually, we had the topmost echelons of authority on the Croatian side, and on our side, in addition to myself, the prime minister, the Minister of Defence, the Minister for Personnel and so forth, and other dignitaries of the HDZ of Bosnia and Herzegovina were about, in addition to me but there were also frequently quite a host of municipal HDZ representatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I hope that clarifies the position so far as we can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Returning shortly to the meeting of the 13th of June itself, was the possibility of the secession of Serbia from the republic reflected in different potential plans or different plans that might be put in place?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: It is true, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what particular plans were considered either at that meeting or at about that time?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: To begin with, that was a time when the presidents of all Yugoslav republics regularly met in the presence of various international representatives. The European union was looking for a formula for a new Yugoslavia, in particular, at that time, so the question of confederation or federation was at the table. Nobody spoke of the independence of individual republics. We, as the leadership of the Republic of Croatia and high dignitaries of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina representing the Croat people, needed to consider all the versions so as not to be taken unawares by the situation. There is no doubt that I and those people who supported me always placed the security and survival of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the forefront, but there were also those who wanted Bosnia-Herzegovina to be no more. When I spoke about the parochial frame of mind, I can corroborate it by saying that very many of them had never heard, let alone observed the Helsinki Act of 1975; they simply wanted to quit Bosnia-Herzegovina. And that kind of policy, which would later on take the upper hand, has inflicted horrendous damage on the Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina, on the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and then on the citizens of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With reference to the two-track approach, or two-track proposal, and reference to a third option, which is the outright secession of the Croatian parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the "two-track" refers, just to be quite clear, to which two proposals?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: One was a sovereign Bosnia-Herzegovina and the equality of the Croat people in it. That was our election platform, on the basis of which we won a landslide victory in the elections. The second presumably spoke of the confederation of Yugoslavia, with individual parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina establishing close ties with their immediate neighbours. And the third option was, if Bosnia-Herzegovina did not survive as a state and if it were divided, what then could Croats be given in it who were not satisfied with the status quo? As with the share of 17,3 per cent of the population, they mostly held underdeveloped and peripheral parts of the republic, and that is why the historical factor was invariably mentioned, because it is a fact that once upon a time, Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina played a much more important role; but owing to two Yugoslavias, the royalist and the communist ones, they were the big victims, and a large number of people emigrated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the third option: Was that discussed at this meeting? Was it ever taken any further by you or by meetings in your presence?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: It was not mentioned openly. Only as a possibility. And I must tell you, because they knew my views they did not discuss it openly before me. But I was not invited to all the meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm turning to another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. That's a convenient moment. Going back to the earlier applications in relation to cross-examination, quite clearly there's a lot of material which this witness has produced --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- quite properly, under the subpoena. There's a question of the amount of time which the Defence need to assimilate it all, if it was given to them over the weekend. So the question of when it's going to be convenient to conduct a cross-examination arises. Obviously, what's got to be balanced is the preparedness of the Defence, the opportunity of which they have, the fact that these documents are not translated, as they will have to be in due course, and it may be more convenient to deal with cross-examination when that is done, as against the convenience of the witness, or the inconvenience to him, being here, as he is, under a subpoena. Now, those are all matters which have got to be balanced, if necessary, by the Court, in making a decision. But it may be sensible for the parties to try and reach a sensible arrangement, bearing in mind the convenience of the witness, as I said. To that end, of course, you may speak to him to ascertain what his position is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I know to some extent what his position is; I've already outlined that. He has to go back on Wednesday; there are things he has to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The documents produced, of course, may by no means all be requiring of cross-examination. They are produced at the moment because he produces them, and there's no real satisfactory way to ensure they're available other than by producing them in the way that I am dealing with it. They were made available on Friday, I think, either for the most part or all of them. I will discuss the matter with my friends over the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, if you would. Very well. We'll adjourn now for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm on paragraph 14 of the summary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two other points, Mr. Kljujic, just to remind the Chamber, or inform them: The Helsinki provisions as to the borders of Bosnia-Herzegovina were what?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: The Conference for European Security, 1975, in which the U.S. and Canada also participated, said that there would be no changes in borders in Europe and that certain ethnic minorities would have guaranteed rights based on high European standards, and it was signed by President Tito of Yugoslavia. All borders were guaranteed, and we received guarantees that the European Community would recognise these borders once the new countries would be recognised, and the Helsinki document would then be signed by every new acceding nation. I later had a meeting with Jacques Santer on 1st March, 1992, when he confirmed this. So the HDZ policy in Bosnia and Herzegovina was for Bosnia and Herzegovina to be recognised in its AVENOJ borders; that is, the borders which it had in the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the 13th of June, 1991, meeting, was there another meeting on the 20th of June in Zagreb with HDZ BiH leaders from Herzegovina, but you weren't present?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: I was not present. A meeting was held on the 20th of June, but I was not even invited to that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the position about documents, just before I return to producing them, is that I think over the weekend, or Friday, documents were produced that it was thought the Prosecution would rely on to some extent, and not all of the documents. It seems to me that that creates a problem, or not a problem, a potential problem, with documents that are untranslated, and it's for that reason that I am simply putting in all the documents, even though we don't rely on them for any particular point, because it's only in this way that I can ensure that material that is not translated and that might assist the Defence is available to them to read. I'm not suggesting the documents have any particular significance, although they might provide a fuller record of the HDZ. That's why I'm doing it very quickly, and it won't necessarily involve time to be taken by either side, but at least the documents are then part of the library of material.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: I should point out that three of the 16 that we've already seen -- in other words, 13 documents that have just been admitted were not delivered to us over the weekend, and as far as we can tell are brand-new.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That may well be the case, for the reason I've just given.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document is 2735, and again, just a "Yes," "No" answer: Is this a minute of --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct, yes. THE FRENCH REPORTER: The interpreter doesn't say who speaks, so I can't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If I am causing problems for the French writer, I apologise. If there is anything I can do to make her task easier, I will do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 2735, extracts from the minutes of the presidency for the 10th of July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes a that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if the Chamber has a view. 2738 is a document that this witness produced to us, but it's already gone in, in, I think, an identical form, as Exhibit Z7. So we can either produce it as part of the series and add to the amount of paper, but that might be more convenient, or we can simply note that it is Z7 and not produce it through this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That seems to be more sensible, the latter course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then we come to 2736, please. Tell us a little bit about this. This is the 31st of July of 1991. Was there a meeting on that day?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I did not attend this meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So far as you know, these are minutes of that meeting, chaired, I think in your absence, by Boban?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turn to the second sheet, please. Can you read out the last three bullet points, as they are known, that come at the end of Tocka 1 and just before Tocka 2?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: It is recognised that the opinion of the Western Herzegovina regional HDZ community coincides with the conclusions of the Travnik Regional Community of the HDZ. Second, it is necessary to consider the possibility of regional linking in other municipalities with majority Croatian population or the communities which are territorially linked with a Croatian population, and the main board is to consider this. Also, the areas where the Croatian population is in minority and territorially is linked, and they can also link to the regional communities of the HDZ in order to have a better-organised and more unified activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any comment to make on those entries or not?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: No. That was the regular organisation of the party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 2739, nothing to say about it, simply that it is a record you produced of the 1st of August, being a press release of the presidency, I think.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes, is it. The document is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document in time, which I needn't produce because it's been dealt with as Exhibit 10 -- I beg your pardon, not through this witness. There is a document Z10 which has already been produced which deals with --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There is a document Z10. I'm sorry. Can it go before the witness? It comes from the core bundle. That's why it's Z10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This reflects a meeting held on the 6th of August, with you in the chair, and again we needn't spend time on this. Does --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes, even though I left the meeting and had to take a helicopter to Sarajevo for urgent state matters, but I do accept the contents of this meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this take further the plans developed in Zagreb on the 13th of June that same year?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: No. I think that this is, first of all, the instructions on what the position should be, given the situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the escalation of the war in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Well, that's available, produced by you. I'm wrong, it wasn't in the core documents. It was one of the library documents given original numbers, and that is available if anybody wants to ask you about it.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: These are minutes from the session which was distributed to all the municipalities in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm grateful. Perhaps if you would like to turn to point 22, which we have in an English translation on this document and which you can -- I know you speak some English indeed, but if you can find it in the original. Paragraph 22 reads, in the English translation: "We remain behind the policy of independence and indivisibility of BH, but should the war start in BH by an attack by a Greater Serbia or any other aggressor on the Croatian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, a special plan will be applied." What plan is that; can you say?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: You see in all the documents, we supported the unity and indivisibility of Bosnia-Herzegovina. However, in case it would not be recognised or not possible, we had to have a plan of protecting the Croatian interest in the pro-Croatian population. And it was against the plan which was called Rame or Frame, which was created by Milosevic, and it had to do with Greater Serbia, which would encompass -- which would go along the lines Zadar on the Adriatic coast, Karlovac, which was 50 kilometres from Zagreb, and Petrinja, also very close to Zagreb. We discovered this plan, and I first -- had it published in the former Yugoslavia and drew attention to Milosevic's plan, because according to this plan, a large segment of the Croatian population in Bosnia-Herzegovina would find itself under the Serbian control, and we could not accept that. This is why we asked that the areas where the Croats were in the majority in this case either become independent or join the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next exhibit needn't be separately produced. It is already Exhibit 11. It is dated the 13th of August. Just tell us what this document is, please, if you can. There is no point I want to make on it, so a sentence to identify what it is is all I ask.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: I believe that this is the implementation, on a regional basis, of certain conclusions reached by the main board of the HDZ BH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. 2741, dated on its last sheet the 17th of August, just tell us what it is. No points to make. Just tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: This was a political platform for rescue of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By what individual or group?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Primarily, against the Serbian fascism and the plan called Rame which I had mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We see a list of names on the fourth sheet, various people, starting with Professor Babic and other professors. Your name is not on it. Any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: This was a meeting of Croat intellectuals who were not politically involved, except for Dr. Komisic, who was the vice-president of the Communists, and perhaps this is the cream of the crop of the Croat intellectuals of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next, 2742, the 23rd of August. I think this is a list of regional communities, and we see Travnik is the first?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document, 2743, a press release dated the 26th of August of the presidency. No points to be made. I'm just producing these documents through you.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: This is just standard minutes, that is, a summary from the presidency meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then the next document is from the Prosecution's original list, Z76,1. Sorry, Z16,1. Is this a document with which you're familiar or not?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: It is the organisational chart of our party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can see that it's dated the 18th of September of 1991 two thirds of the way down the page, and can you just explain the top line, please, for us? The presidency is identified by its constituent members, hierarchy?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We see your name as the president. Can you put it a little higher up on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other members are shown as Mate Boban and Vlado Santic as vice-presidents, Markesic as --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Secretary general.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then Kostroman as secretary?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next row signifies what?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: This is the main board, some kind of a greater council, the largest collective body in the party, and the presidents of all sizeable organisations were represented here, for the most part, where the Croats were in a position of authority in local governments or where they had very significant minorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then the bottom part of the chart underneath the date, the box with the date, what's that about?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: We had a security council for the HDZ and a crisis staff, which consisted of myself as president, Mate Boban as vice-president, and our officials who were in the government, Branko Kvesic and Bruno Stojic in the Ministry of Interior, Jerko Doko, Ministry of Defence, and some prominent persons from the different regions. We all sought to have all regions represented in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then we see Dario Kordic's name here, bottom left-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this crisis staff, not as a representative of one of the municipalities on the main board?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: He was the representative of several municipalities from the Travnik region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. 2745, no points. 18th of September. It's the conclusions of, I think, is it the security council of HDZ BH?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Back to paragraph 16 in the summary. Was there a meeting on the 8th of October of 1991?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm afraid I can't help you with that. Maybe the date is wrong.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: But a meeting of what body, presidency?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Presidency and crisis staff. Maybe we should go back to the last -- here it is.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: It's possible there was a regular routine meeting of the presidency and the crisis staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This one, I think, has not been copied. Can I lay it on the ELMO and it will be copied? It's our Exhibit Z18.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take your time to look at this. This is, of course, in English, but assuming that it is a proper reflection of a document in B/C/S, it reflects a meeting on the 8th of October of the joint meeting of the presidency and the crisis staff. It sets out some conclusions. Would you turn to number 7 of the conclusions and see if you can help us with that? Is the B/C/S attached to that? Don't attach it at the moment. Just show the B/C/S number 7 on the ELMO, please. Can you put it up so that we can follow it?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is correct, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read number 7 and it will be translated for us, and then we'll get it properly copied?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: "Persons appointed to state organs by the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina shall continue to perform their duties conscientiously, thinking first and foremost of the interests of the Croatian people."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And any more?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Do you want a comment on this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read the totality of number 7 first?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: "Inasmuch as the work of our representatives referred to in the above paragraph is paralysed, all our representatives in organs of authority shall withdraw therefrom, and in that case the sole legitimate representatives of the Croatian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina shall be the presidency of the BH HDZ and the BH HDZ crisis staff of the republic, as well as our municipal and intermunicipal authorities where we are in the majority. "In the event of the withdrawal of the representatives of the BH HDZ from organs of authority in the republic, a special plan in work in extraordinary circumstances shall be drafted."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any comment you want to make on that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: At that time, the Serbian representatives in the government were paralysing the joint work of the institutions of Bosnia and Herzegovina so that the joint institutions were unable to run the country efficiently. In practical terms, everyone was doing what they wanted, and the intention here was to gather together all the representatives of the Croats and the party leadership so that should a new situation arise, since we had our election results, they and only they could represent the will and the interests of the Croatian people. With this, we wanted to prevent any possible misuse of the Communist Party which might, in a rump assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, try to contribute to the out-voting of Croats, since we were the smallest of all the three national parties, so that when we say that our representatives must perform their duties conscientiously, this means that they should work honestly within the republic institutions, bearing in mind the Croats, if a situation of confusion should arise.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. That document, Your Honour, has been produced already as Exhibit Z18 through an earlier witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 17 of the summary. Did problems develop in the Travnik region, later the Travnik Regional Community?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: What kind of problems are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's deal with it in another way. Did there come a time when you required Mr. Kordic to come to the party headquarters in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: There were several complaints about his attitude. I did not consider this to be particularly important because in the government bodies of Bosnia and Herzegovina we had numerous problems in the Ministry of Defence, the Ministry of the Interior, and I simply required discipline in the field so that we could work seriously. I think that at one moment I was very energetic in demanding absolute obedience from Mr. Kordic, because the worst thing that could have happened to us at that moment would have been if, instead of global interests, we started dealing with local conflicts of a personal kind. However, what I said then was simply in an outburst of anger. I did not really mean it seriously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you said was what, just so we have the detail? What was it you said, the detail?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: I should say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Well, I said I would have him arrested because he was causing problems for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I needn't trouble with the next exhibit in the bundle, Z18,1. We can turn to the 11th of November of 1991, Mr. Kljuic. On that day, was something called the Croatian Community of Bosnia Posavina created?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, since the situation was very complicated, the war was raging in Croatia, many troops of the Yugoslav army arrived in Bosnia from Slovenia, from parts of Croatia, and reservists and volunteers were called in from Yugoslavia and Montenegro from Serbia. At that time, Bosnia and Herzegovina was the biggest military barracks in Europe, and we had 17 Corps of the JNA which was extremely well armed in classical weapons. It was impossible from Sarajevo, because we had difficulties with telephone connections, our telephones were bugged.
